entry.name: DexTacWAM
entry.title: DexTacWAM: A Visuo-Tactile World-Action Model for Dexterous Manipulation
entry.summary: Two 22-DoF Sharpa Wave hands on a teleoperated Dexmate torso, recorded with ten fingertip gel images, marker-flow fields and 6-axis wrenches per frame over a 488-episode pretraining corpus and six task sets of 96-100 demonstrations.
entry.hand: Sharpa Wave (22 DoF) x 2 on a Dexmate dual-arm torso (7 arm joints per side); 3 of the 6 task sets use the right hand only

sensor.note: Five fingertip sensors per hand (thumb, index, middle, ring, pinky). LeRobot sets, per sensor and frame: 'tactile' grayscale gel image 192x256 uint8 (the raw sensor image is 240x320), 'tactile_flow' 24x32 grid x (dx, dy, magnitude, divergence) float32, precomputed; task sets also 'deform' 192x256 uint8 deformation map (zero outside contact in the checked episode). The 10 x 6-axis fingertip wrenches are not a separate column: they are actions[0:60]. Raw HDF5 repos: tactile_raw (5, 240, 320), tactile_deform (5, 240, 240) uint8 and tactile_f6 (5, 6) float32 per hand at 30 Hz. No palm or phalanx sensing.

scale.text: 1,083 episodes, 655,562 frames (~6.1 h) @30 fps: 488-episode pretraining corpus (250 instructions, 3.5 h) + 6 task sets of 96-100 demos (595 episodes, 2.6 h); 4 more raw HDF5 repos (300 success + 40 failure episodes) outside the collection

entry.access: Hugging Face collection JensenYuan/dextacwam: 7 ungated LeRobot v2.1 repos (~509 GB, one parquet per episode with images and tactile arrays inside); 4 raw HDF5 + MP4 repos (~305 GB) sit under the same account but are not in the collection or README.
caveats: The 488-episode pretraining corpus re-releases T-Rex recordings (same lab, rig and 21 of T-Rex's 22 motor-primitive verbs): in 48 of 48 checked episodes the 58-D joint-state range lies inside a T-Rex episode with the same primitive and object (2 identical in length and range; corpus 200 = T-Rex 3479 frame for frame). The authors do not say this; it is the catalog's check.

Fingertip wrenches are stored inside 'actions' (first 60 values: left then right hand, thumb..pinky, 6 values each), unit not stated; frames where a finger read all zeros were filled with the previous value during conversion.
Tactile and camera images are downscaled to 192x256 (raw gel image 240x320, raw cameras 640x360). The 488 corpus has the head camera only and no 'deform' column.
Three task sets (unstack bowl, place with tongs, pick-place cube) are right hand only: tactile (1, 5, 192, 256), state 45, actions 75, no left wrist camera.

State and action layouts differ between the 488 corpus (state 58 = joints; actions 136) and the task sets (state 90 / actions 150 bimanual, 45 / 75 right-only, with 4x4 end-effector poses); see data/utils/layout_contracts/arm_layouts.json in the code.

Converted sets hold successful demonstrations only; the raw repos also hold 40 failure episodes, have no dataset card or license tag, and two of them (pick cherry tomato with tong, pick cube in a bag) have no converted counterpart.
Episodes are single-row-group parquet files of 33 MB to 2.5 GB with PNG frames and uint8 arrays inside (no MP4), so one episode's tactile cannot be fetched without its whole column chunk.
207 of the 250 corpus instructions have 1-2 episodes (max 6); the card says there are too few episodes per task to train a policy from it.

unconfirmed: hours=6.1, episodes=1,083, frames=655,562 summed from meta/episodes.jsonl of the 7 collection repos: 488 corpus 377,788 frames (3.50 h); bottle cap 96 / 58,064; bowl 100 / 36,712; tongs 100 / 55,691; handover 100 / 34,218; wipe 99 / 66,185; cube place 100 / 26,904 (task sets 595 / 277,774 = 2.57 h). Paper and project page say 'roughly four hours' for the corpus; its card says 3.5 h. The 4 raw repos (wipe 100+13 failure, pick cube right hand 100+5, cherry tomato with tong 50+11, cube in a bag 50+11) are not counted; 2 of them are the sources of converted sets (dataset_identity.json source_data_dir).

tasks=256 = 250 distinct corpus instructions (meta/tasks.jsonl) + 6 evaluation tasks. The corpus instructions use 21 primitive verbs (lift and place, wrap, fold, grasp and lifting, close, press, open, peel, reach, wipe, squeeze, cut, insert, pour, extract, screw, shake, dispense, assemble, twist, disassemble) over 210 distinct object phrases; objects left null because no count is published.

T-Rex overlap: 48 corpus episodes (12 chosen + 36 random, seed 0) had their per-dimension state min/max compared with T-Rex meta/episodes per-episode observation.state min/max (both 58-D, layout [L_arm 7, L_hand 22, R_arm 7, R_hand 22]). Every one lies inside a T-Rex episode whose motor_primitive and object match the corpus instruction (47 inside exactly one, 1 inside five incl. the matching one); episodes 200 (= T-Rex 3479, grasp and lift shoes, 555 frames) and 396 (= T-Rex 513, keyboard, 447 frames) match exactly, the rest are shorter, i.e. trimmed. The corpus metadata backup is dated 2026-05-21, before T-Rex appeared on HF (2026-06-11). Task strings differ (corpus 'verb object' vs T-Rex captions). The six task sets are not in T-Rex (3 checked episodes: no containing T-Rex episode; collected 2026-07-24 to 08-09 per directory names). Frame-level check (2026-10-17): corpus episode 200 observation 'state' equals T-Rex episode 3479 'observation.state' in all 555 frames (max abs difference 0.0).

SharpaDex v1.0 overlap: none found. SharpaDex uses a 65-D state with torso joints and 4 RGB cameras and is collected by Sharpa; DexTacWAM uses 58/90-D states and 3 cameras. Only the task name 'unscrew bottle cap' is shared. No episode-level comparison was made.

Robot: the card says 'Dexmate torso with two Sharpa Wave dexterous hands' and the README 'dexmate the 22-DoF bimanual robot'; the Dexmate model (Vega-1 in T-Rex) is not named. Camera models not stated (T-Rex, same rig: ZED X Mini head, ZED X One S wrists).

Wrench: actions[0:60] equals raw HDF5 left/right_hand_tactile_f6 except in filled dropout frames (wipe_whiteboard ep 0 vs raw episode_0004: 213 of 39,780 cells differ, each a held previous value). Component order (Fx, Fy, Fz, Mx, My, Mz) assumed from T-Rex's f6 naming; unit not stated, values quantized to 0.01 with |F| peaks of 13-23 in sampled episodes, i.e. plausibly N. Right-hand |F| reaches 21.0 in several bowl episodes (possible clip, not checked).

Tactile image size: 192x256 is 0.8x of the raw 240x320 gel image; the resize itself was not traced in code (vtam_data_scripts is not released). deform 192x256 comes from the raw 240x240 map, so it is stretched or padded (not checked). tactile_flow channel order (dx, dy, magnitude, divergence) is from data/tactile_dataset.py; unit not stated.

Raw cameras: ffprobe of pick_cube_right_hand_raw episode_0001 head_left_rgb and left_wrist MP4s: H.264 High 4:4:4 Predictive (lossless-style, gbrp), 640x360, 30 fps, 298 frames = total_steps. Raw HDF5 timestamp steps median 33.9 ms (command_hz 30).

488 corpus actions (136) layout read from values: [0:60] wrench, [60:76] and [76:92] two 4x4 target poses (last row 0 0 0 1), [92:136] 44 hand joint targets; no arm joint targets. Task-set layout from arm_layouts.json and verified against raw HDF5 (state joints exact, poses and targets < 2e-7).

Teleoperation: paper says demonstrations are 'visuo-tactile teleoperation demonstrations'; the device for the fingers is not stated. Raw HDF5 holds left/right_vive_pose (HTC Vive assumed from the name).

download.format: LeRobot v2.1 (no videos): data/chunk-000/episode_XXXXXX.parquet, one row group per episode, holding PNG frames (head_img, *_wrist_img), uint8 tactile/deform arrays and float32 tactile_flow; meta/{info.json, episodes.jsonl, episodes_stats.jsonl, tasks.jsonl}; task sets add dataset_identity.json, conversion_metadata.json, episode_provenance.json. Raw repos: <success|failure>/episode_NNNN/{episode_NNNN.h5, *_head_left_rgb.mp4, *_left_wrist.mp4, *_right_wrist.mp4}.
download.total_size: ~509 GB in the collection by HF tree sizes (488 corpus 302.6, bottle cap 52.1, bowl 18.8, tongs 27.9, handover 32.9, wipe 60.6, cube place 14.3 GB): 467.4 GB episode parquet + 41.7 GB episodes_stats.jsonl (the 488 corpus carries it twice, in meta/ and meta.bak.20260521_212738/); the cards quote 282 GB and 13-57 GB. Raw repos: 305 GB more
download.per_episode: parquet median ~495 MB (488 corpus, 33 MB-2.5 GB); task sets median 121 MB (cube place) to 571 MB (wipe); raw HDF5 0.4-2.4 GB + 3 MP4s of 25-165 MB
download.partial_fetch: single files via https://huggingface.co/datasets/JensenYuan/<repo>/resolve/main/<path>; HTTP range reads of the footer + small column chunks (state, actions incl. wrench, timestamp: < 0.1 MB per episode); tactile, deform and image columns are one chunk per episode (24-49 MB tactile for 180-246 frames). Raw HDF5 is chunked and range-readable with h5py.

sample.reason: Apache-2.0 on every collection card ('Apache 2.0, matching the DexTacWAM code ... that restriction applies to those source files, not to this data'); all repos are public and ungated and single parquet files download through resolve URLs. Label the collection 'Apache-2.0'. Episodes come from the six task sets only: the 488-episode corpus re-releases trimmed T-Rex recordings (48 of 48 checked), which the viewer already shows under tr_.

episodes.task: Unscrew the cap off the bottle and set it down.
episodes.subject: robot: Dexmate + 2x Sharpa Wave, teleoperated
episodes.why: Twist, two hands. Wrench |F| more than 1 above rest for 5.6-6.6 s continuous on left index, middle and ring (holding the bottle, peaks 12.5-20.8) and 1.1-1.2 s on right thumb and index (turning the cap, peaks 20.3 / 13.4); contact 2.4-10.3 s. Strongest of the 4 smallest episodes of 10-60 s checked.

episodes.task: Hold the lower bowls with the right thumb, lift the edge of the top bowl with the index or middle finger, slide the thumb over, then pinch and lift the top bowl.
episodes.subject: robot: right hand only
episodes.why: Friction-driven separation, one hand. Thumb 2.1 s (peak 17.5) and index 1.8 s (peak 14.7) above rest + 1, contact 4.8-8.7 s. Chosen over episodes 39 and 96 (longer thumb contact) because their thumb peaks sit at exactly 21.0, a possible clip.

episodes.task: Grasp the cherry tomato with the tongs, move it over the plate, then release it.
episodes.subject: robot: right hand only
episodes.why: Tool use, one hand. Thumb, index and middle stay above rest + 1 for 7.7 / 7.3 / 7.5 s (peaks 17.7 / 11.5 / 13.1) while squeezing the tongs, contact 3.8-12.0 s; pinky also touches (0.7 s).

episodes.task: Pick up the cube with the right hand and hand it over to the left hand.
episodes.subject: robot: both hands
episodes.why: Hand-to-hand transfer. Right thumb and middle 4.3 s (peaks 19.2 / 10.8), left thumb, index and middle 2.5-2.7 s (peaks 11.6-14.6), contact 3.3-9.6 s; both hands in contact during the transfer.

episodes.task: Hold the white board with the left hand and wipe it clean with the eraser in the right hand.
episodes.subject: robot: both hands
episodes.why: Sustained two-hand contact (wipe). Left thumb/index 9.7 / 9.4 s holding the board (peaks 22.5 / 15.9), right thumb/index/middle 5.4-6.4 s on the eraser (peaks 21.3 / 7.2 / 7.1); the smallest file of the set.

episodes.task: Pick up the cube from the right side of the table with the right hand and place it in the middle.
episodes.subject: robot: right hand only, head camera occluded by the arm
episodes.why: Grasp and place, one hand. Thumb 2.7 s (peak 11.8), pinky 2.5 s (peak 5.5) and ring 1.5 s above rest + 1, contact 5.6-8.7 s. Only 300 frames: most episodes of this set are under 10 s (median 259 frames).

sample.fetch_estimate: ~1.4 GB: the 6 whole parquet files (291 + 141 + 182 + 257 + 403 + 140 MB, HF tree sizes); tactile, deform and PNG image columns are one chunk per episode, so partial fetch saves little. Re-hosted media: head + wrist PNG frames re-encoded to H.264 (192x256, 300-471 frames, ~1-3 MB per view); the ten 192x256 gel images per frame need either a tactile video or a reduced grid, estimate ~5-15 MB per episode as H.264. Episode JSON: 60 wrench values x <= 471 frames, well below 2 MB; tactile_flow (24x32x4 per sensor) would exceed 2 MB per episode at full rate and has to be reduced (e.g. per-sensor mean |flow| series) or shown as video.
sample.rules_applied: Tasks: 256 task strings (250 corpus instructions + 6 evaluation tasks), so 6-8 are taken; the 6 evaluation task sets are all taken (twist, friction-based separation, tool use, handover, wipe, pick-place; 3 two-handed, 3 one-handed; bottle, bowls, tongs + tomato, cube, whiteboard + eraser). Corpus instructions are not taken: their recordings are already in the catalog through T-Rex. Episodes: one per sampled task, 6 in total. Candidates: the 4 smallest parquet files with 300-1,800 frames (10-60 s) per set; contact = per-fingertip |F| (actions wrench, first 3 components) more than 1 above the median of the first 15 frames, longest contiguous run reported. Every pick has at least one fingertip in contact for 1.8 s or more. No window cut: all are 10.0-15.7 s. Budget: 6 episodes, ~1.4 GB download, under the 20 GB limit.

checks.method: Actions column (wrench) of 24 task-set episodes range-read from the parquet footers (scan in the survey's scratch dir); tactile, deform, tactile_flow and images checked in pick_place_cube episode 34 only; wrench and joints checked against raw HDF5 in wipe_whiteboard episode 0.
checks.not_checked: tactile and deform columns of the 6 picked episodes (presence assumed from info.json: every episode has the columns); left/right orientation of the gel images; whether |F| = 21.0 is a sensor clip.
